svg.title: Result: paper grade
svg.text: MPX SPIN V1 (CONCEPT 04 DEVELOPED) · DESIGN REVIEW
Result 2 · Paper grade: catching small particles costs flow

text.tspan: Four plain cellulose papers in the same Spin v1 at 1,500 rpm with vanes. Finer papers catch far more by count, but pass less water and clog sooner.

svg.text: Capture by count (1–100 µm) vs batch-cycle flow
small dots: same paper without vanes

text.tspan: Grade 4 is the rig's paper. The < 2 µm Grade 602 h class is the only one inside the target zone; Grade 5
(2.5 µm) is tighter in Herzberg time but rated coarser, so it catches less and flows less.

svg.text: THE FOUR PAPERS AT 1,500 RPM WITH VANES

text.tspan: Face × is the same for all four: it is just the wall pressure divided by the rating test's 10 cm head,
whatever the paper. Sleeve L is tap water until the cycle falls below 15 L/h.

svg.text: THE CONTRADICTION TO CARRY INTO TRIZ

text.tspan: particles needs a tighter paper, which cuts flow and sleeve life. Spin v1 sits at
in that band: just short of 90 %. Going tighter means going faster, a bigger sleeve or a
